_note: Own library, written for this skill. A direction is a way of composing a page (an idea engine), not a look. Palettes and type are dealt separately.

directions.name: Type specimen
directions.engine: The subject's name or one word of its vocabulary is set so large it becomes the picture.
directions.hero: One word or name filling 70 to 100% of the viewport width, cropped or tightly set; one sentence and one action beside or under it. No picture is required.
directions.sections: Alternate full-width specimen lines with ruled-off content blocks of plain text; vary the specimen size section to section.
directions.risks: Needs a name or word with character; a long generic name defeats it. Headline-lines check will fire on purpose here: use a one-line specimen and keep the real h1 short.
directions.disagrees: A one-word hero is under the usual headline size floor in the other direction: it is far above it, so hero-size never fires, but check that the supporting sentence stays visible.

directions.name: The printed thing
directions.engine: The page is built as the printed object of the subject's world: a ticket, menu, label, timetable, receipt, invitation, manual.
directions.hero: The artefact itself at reading size, on a plain field, carrying the real headline and the primary action as parts of it (a ticket stub is the button).
directions.sections: Each section is a different region or fold of the same object; keep its real conventions (columns of a timetable, dotted leaders on a menu).
directions.risks: A skeuomorphic texture becomes ornament; take the structure and typography of the object, not its paper texture.
directions.disagrees: Dotted leaders, tabular rules and small caps are normal here; they are structure, not decoration.

directions.name: Object cutaway
directions.engine: One physical object or its silhouette, enlarged and cropped, is the frame; copy attaches to its parts.
directions.hero: The object occupies 55 to 70% of the first screen, cropped by the edge; headline overlaps its quiet area, never its detail.
directions.sections: Move the camera: each section crops a different part of the same object, text attached to the part it explains.
directions.risks: Needs a strong real or well-drawn object; a stock product shot kills it.
directions.disagrees: Callout lines to parts of the object are structure; keep them only where they point at something.

directions.name: Ledger
directions.engine: The subject's real numbers are the layout: a table, a column of figures, a price list that is the design.
directions.hero: One decisive figure at display size with its unit and what it means, next to a plain table of the other figures.
directions.sections: Rows and columns throughout; one section per question the numbers answer, each opening with the figure.
directions.risks: Invented numbers are forbidden: only real figures from the brief; otherwise pick another direction.
directions.disagrees: Hairline row rules and tabular figures are normal; thin rules elsewhere are not.

directions.name: Route
directions.engine: A real map, route or timeline is the spine of the page; sections are stops along it.
directions.hero: The map or line, large, with the subject's place marked; headline sits in a clear quadrant.
directions.sections: The route continues through the page as a vertical line or progress mark; each stop has a place, a time or a distance in its heading.
directions.risks: A decorative line with no real stops is an ornament; every stop must be a real place, step or date.
directions.disagrees: A continuous line is a thin rule by the meter; here it is the structure, so keep it single and meaningful.

directions.name: Archive wall
directions.engine: Found pictures of the subject's world, hung and captioned like museum labels, carry the page.
directions.hero: One archival picture at 45 to 60% of the first screen with a caption that states what it is, plus the headline.
directions.sections: Picture-led blocks of varied sizes; each caption names the subject, date and source; copy is short and sits beside the picture.
directions.risks: Found pictures show the world around the client, never the client's own product or people; credits go in the footer.
directions.disagrees: Dense image grids are normal here; the fullness check passes easily, so judge rhythm by eye.

directions.name: Ritual
directions.engine: The page performs the subject's real sequence as the visitor scrolls: a process, a day, a recipe, a season.
directions.hero: Step one of the sequence, shown and named; a visible sign that there is more (the next hour, the next stage).
directions.sections: One screen per step, each changing one dominant thing; numbers are allowed because the content is a real sequence.
directions.risks: Scroll-jacking: the page must read fully with motion off and without script.
directions.disagrees: Numbered markers are legitimate here; confirm the content is truly ordered.

directions.name: Split world
directions.engine: Two halves of the subject's world sit side by side (before and after, day and night, two audiences) and the page lets one answer the other.
directions.hero: The first screen is cut in two with a different ground, type size and content on each side; the headline crosses the seam.
directions.sections: Each section re-uses the seam: the two halves stay opposed (problem and answer, then and now) until the final section joins them.
directions.risks: On a phone the halves stack; the seam must still read as a contrast, not as two unrelated blocks.
directions.disagrees: Two competing focal points are intended in the hero; one must still win by size.

directions.name: Fields of colour
directions.engine: Whole full-bleed fields of one colour per section, with type and one object, carry the page; no cards, no borders.
directions.hero: A full-bleed colour field with the headline at display size and one object or cut-out placed off-centre.
directions.sections: Each section its own field from the palette, edge to edge; type changes size, not decoration, between fields.
directions.risks: Needs a palette with real contrast between fields; pastel sets blur into each other.
directions.disagrees: Large flat fills are intended; the gradient and shadow checks should stay quiet.

directions.name: Manual
directions.engine: The page reads like an instruction booklet or exploded diagram of the subject.
directions.hero: A large diagram or exploded view of the subject, drawn in the palette's colours, with the headline plainly set beside it.
directions.sections: Diagram plus a short numbered procedure per section; callouts only on parts that matter.
directions.risks: A diagram that is not accurate to the subject is decoration; draw it from real parts or do not use this direction.
directions.disagrees: Numbered callouts are structure here, but only where the content is a procedure.

directions.name: Live instrument
directions.engine: The hero is a working instrument of the subject: a configurator, calculator, availability or status display.
directions.hero: The instrument itself on the first screen with sane real defaults and its result stated in large type; headline names what it answers.
directions.sections: Each section explains or extends one control of the instrument; the instrument state follows into the final action.
directions.risks: Must work with a thumb and have a plain fallback; fake data that cannot be real is worse than no instrument.
directions.disagrees: Dense control panels are normal inside the instrument; the rest of the page stays spacious.

directions.name: Correspondence
directions.engine: The page is a set of notes, letters or postcards from the subject to the visitor, written in a human voice.
directions.hero: A short letter set like a letter (paragraph, signature, date) at reading size, with the action as its closing line.
directions.sections: Each section is another note with its own date or place; handwriting-like type only for annotations, never for body text.
directions.risks: Twee voice; keep it factual and specific, and avoid fake personal stories.
directions.disagrees: Long paragraphs in the hero are intended; keep the h1 short and above them.

directions.name: Poster stack
directions.engine: Every section is a poster: one dominant thing and the content it carries, full screen, no two alike.
directions.hero: A poster composition: one dominant element at 50% or more of the screen, headline integrated with it.
directions.sections: Each section is its own poster with its own dominant element, size and alignment.
directions.risks: Needs real content for every poster; empty posters are the near-empty screens the meter fails.
directions.disagrees: Strong asymmetry is intended; the frame check can warn: defend it or close the void.

palettes.proportions: 70 ground, 20 field, 8 ink, 2 accent. The accent appears once per screen.
75 ground, 15 field, 8 ink, 2 accent. Blue only on actions and one figure.
60 ground, 25 field, 10 ink, 5 accent. Never pair with a serif display plus terracotta: that is the common default.
40 ground, 40 field, 15 ink, 5 accent. Full yellow fields are the point; keep ink at full strength.
65 ground, 25 field, 8 ink, 2 accent. Gold is a hairline use, never a fill.
80 ground, 10 field, 8 ink, 2 accent. Warm paper only if the subject is print or paper.
50 ground, 35 field, 12 ink, 3 accent. Check the accent against the field: contrast above 3:1.
75 ground, 15 field, 8 ink, 2 accent. Acid accent is a known default; use it only if the subject owns that color.
50 ground, 30 field, 15 ink, 5 accent. Name the subject's own fruit, wood or soil colors instead if it has them.

type.note: Display at weight 700 and tight tracking; body serif at 18 to 20px, line height 1.55.
One family: weight and size carry hierarchy; display at 600 and a size jump of at least 3x over body.
Serif only for the statement; avoid italic on a single word of the headline.
A monospace (IBM Plex Mono) is allowed for real data, code or figures; not for decorative labels.
Condensed display at huge sizes, never in running text; body at 17px minimum.
Fraunces with the soft optical axis; do not combine with a cream and terracotta page.
Rounded feel suits services and education; keep weights to 400 and 700.
A book setting: generous leading (1.6), measure under 70 characters, small caps only for real abbreviations.
Use the width axis for display (Archivo Expanded at 700), normal width for body.

features.text: One large picture of the subject with 3 to 5 labels attached to real parts; no icon grid.
Alternating picture and text rows with a full paragraph each; the picture varies in crop and size.
A single column list where every item pairs the claim with its proof (a figure, a photo, a quote).

how-it-works.text: One screen per step, the dominant element changes each time; numbers allowed because it is a real sequence.
One real example walked through end to end, with the actual inputs and outputs shown.
A vertical spine with dated or timed stops and the artefact each step produces.

proof.text: One real outcome stated with its figure and source; no logo strip.
Raw material shown unedited (a real message, a real invoice, a real screen) with a one-line caption.
Only real mentions, linked; if there are none, leave the section out.

pricing.text: One price stated big, with exactly what it includes and what it does not.
A plain table by need (not by tier names), each row with its price and who it suits.
No fixed prices: a short form that states the real range and the response time.

faq.text: Real questions as headings with full answers, all visible; no accordion that hides content from search.
Questions split by audience (before buying, after buying), each answer two to four sentences.
The five questions that come up most, answered as a short transcript in the subject's own voice.

gallery.text: A grid of frames at one size, captions below with title, year and technique.
One piece per screen, full width, caption set small underneath.
A wall of varied sizes with captions as museum labels.

cta.text: One sentence, one button named for what it does, one line about what happens next.
The hero's device returns, resolved: the ticket gets torn, the instrument shows the final result.
The real contact details (address, hours, phone) set big, with the map.

footer.text: Credits, licences, the fonts and pictures used, the real address; written plainly.
Complete navigation plus one contact method; legal links present and real.
A last line in display size that echoes the idea, with the small print beneath.
